The slide should be designed exclusively for audience comprehension; speaker cues and talking points belong only in separate notes, never visible on the slide itself.

tensions.guidance: Default to keeping the audience-facing slide free of speaker-cue text (the majority position) for investor and science decks, and route presenter cues to a presenter-notes view the audience never sees; this preserves eye contact without requiring the slide itself to carry redundant cue text.
tensions.resolution: Kept as resolved in stage 2: no presenter cue text on audience-facing slides. Cues go to presenter notes.

rules.rule: When a draft section is unclear or hard to follow, diagnose it as a gap in the underlying problem-solving logic rather than a wording problem.
rules.applies_when: a slide, section, or note reads as unclear or confusing
rules.check: can you state the precise problem, trace every root cause behind it, and confirm each conclusion follows from that analysis? If not, the fix is structural, not a rewrite
rules.prevents: wasted revision effort polishing sentences when the real defect is incomplete or disordered thinking

rules.rule: Never group an action or recommendation with the result it produces as if they were parallel, equal-level points.
rules.applies_when: a slide or section lists steps, causes, or recommendations alongside their outcomes
rules.check: for each bullet, label it as either an action to take or a result to expect, and confirm actions and results sit at different structural levels
rules.prevents: confusion about what is being recommended versus what will happen as a consequence

rules.rule: For any causal or pattern claim, verify the draft doesn't confuse correlation with causation, ignore bias or confounds, skip a needed comparison or control, overgeneralize past the sample, or wave away a real pattern as chance.
rules.applies_when: a claim attributes a cause to an effect or asserts a trend from data
rules.check: walk each causal or trend claim through the checklist: causation vs. correlation, bias/confound check, comparison or control present, sample scope matches claim scope, pattern vs. chance addressed
rules.prevents: invalid conclusions that damage credibility and create liability risk

merged_from.rule: Before using statistical or comparative evidence to support a claim, check it for confounding variables that could change its interpretation; for a specifically causal claim about what produced an improvement, prefer evidence where the compared conditions differ only in the one feature being credited.
merged_from.check: identify variables that could alter interpretation of the statistic and confirm the evidence addresses or discloses them; for causal claims, confirm the comparison holds other factors constant and varies only the credited feature

merged_from.rule: When a slide asserts that one thing causes another, confirm the evidence rules out the reverse direction and name the specific kind of relationship rather than treating all links as generically the same.
merged_from.check: the evidence shown distinguishes correlation from causation and from reverse causality; the slide or notes specify what kind of relationship (direct, delayed, mutual) is being claimed

rules.rule: Avoid an explicit problem-diagnosis walkthrough when the people in the room are responsible for causing the problem.
rules.applies_when: the audience includes people whose decisions created the problem being discussed
rules.check: verify the audience list; if it includes those responsible, restructure the narrative to avoid walking through root causes in front of them
rules.prevents: defensiveness that undermines acceptance of the recommendation

rules.rule: Before finalizing, confirm the core claim precisely answers the opening question and that every supporting idea provably adds distinct value.
rules.applies_when: before a draft is finalized
rules.check: state the opening question, confirm the core claim answers it directly, and confirm removing any supporting idea would lose something; cut any idea that doesn't
rules.prevents: shipping a deck with a wandering opening or supporting points that don't earn their place

rules.rule: In a deck built for live delivery, treat body text that would make a slide fully understandable as a standalone document, or a deck that feels comprehensive and complete, as a sign of overload. Move the surplus to notes or appendix. This does not apply to the primary visual, which should still be readable on its own (DSN-56), or to read-alone variants.
rules.applies_when: reviewing the live variant of a deck for density
rules.check: confirm each slide requires the speaker's narration to be fully understood, and the deck includes only what's essential to the audience's decision; everything else moves to the appendix
rules.prevents: slides that function as documents instead of visual anchors, and audiences who read ahead instead of listening
curation: Rescoped to live body text. Unscoped, it contradicted SPW-04, SPW-19, and DSN-56.

rules.rule: Don't flatten or restructure a complex claim just to fit a template's default layout.
rules.applies_when: a slide's required content or structure doesn't fit the chosen template
rules.check: confirm the layout was adapted to the message's actual complexity rather than the message being cut or simplified to fit the layout
rules.prevents: oversimplification or loss of meaning driven by template constraints rather than the content's needs

rules.rule: Justify every piece of content kept on a slide by how it supports the core claim, not by fear of leaving something out, anticipating every possible question, or attachment to the work.
rules.applies_when: deciding what stays on a slide or in the main deck
rules.check: for each item under consideration, confirm the stated reason for keeping it is its contribution to the core message, not anxiety or pride
rules.prevents: overloaded slides and decisions driven by fear rather than strategy

rules.rule: Keep opening slides and opening speaker notes free of apologies or disclaimers about preparation.
rules.applies_when: writing the opening slide or its speaker notes
rules.check: confirm no apology or self-deprecating disclaimer about readiness or preparation appears in the opening material
rules.prevents: undermining presenter credibility before the core message is delivered

rules.rule: Before applying visual design, animation, or template polish, confirm the claim, evidence, and information structure are already sound.
rules.applies_when: a slide is being styled, animated, or otherwise visually refined
rules.check: confirm the underlying argument and structure were validated before polish was applied; no polish should appear on a slide whose claim or evidence is still weak or incomplete
rules.prevents: wasting design effort trying to make a substantively weak slide look convincing, which reads as masking weak substance
rules.note: merged near-duplicate rules from three authors arguing polish cannot substitute for weak structure or weak arguments

rules.rule: When resolving feedback that asks for more visual polish, check whether the underlying claim is actually unclear before adding polish.
rules.applies_when: incorporating reviewer or stakeholder feedback on a draft
rules.check: confirm revisions made in response to 'make it more polished' feedback address a clarity or evidence gap, not just a visual preference
rules.prevents: over-designing a slide in response to preference ratings while the actual decision-relevant content stays unclear

rules.rule: Never distort a chart's scale, baseline, or proportions to make the data visually reinforce the claim more than the numbers support.
rules.applies_when: building any chart
rules.check: confirm axis scales start and increment in a way that represents the data honestly, with no stretched, truncated, or non-linear scale chosen to amplify an effect
rules.prevents: a single detected distortion discrediting the whole argument

rules.rule: Never use flashing, blinking, or rapidly flickering effects to draw attention to a slide element.
rules.applies_when: choosing an emphasis or transition effect
rules.check: confirm no element in the deck flashes or blinks
rules.prevents: reduced comprehension and retention caused by flashing effects

rules.rule: Don't constrain slide design to the 'seven words per bullet, seven bullets per slide' formula.
rules.applies_when: deciding slide length or bullet count
rules.check: confirm layout and content decisions are driven by what the claim needs, not by a fixed word- or bullet-count target
rules.prevents: applying an unsupported, arbitrary design constraint instead of the deck's actual content needs

rules.rule: Flag claim or evidence language that doesn't evoke a concrete, visualizable picture.
rules.applies_when: writing a slide claim or a speaker note
rules.check: ask whether a reader could picture what's being described; purely abstract phrasing with no concrete referent should be flagged for rewriting
rules.prevents: prose that technically states a point but fails to actually land it with the audience
